thread.title: Build D2 Architecture Studio
thread.preview: D2 **v0.9.0 requires Go 1.27.0 or newer**, according to its [`go.mod`](https://github.com/d2lang/d2/blob/v0.9.0/go.mod).

content.text: which go version d2 0.9.0 needs? brief

items.text: D2 **v0.9.0 requires Go 1.27.0 or newer**, according to its [`go.mod`](https://github.com/d2lang/d2/blob/v0.9.0/go.mod).

Created the first :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}[D2 web-port audit](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/08ce5f4a74a0/D2-Web-Port-Audit.md). The application is unchanged.

It maps:

- D2’s pipeline from parsing through rendering.
- Shape and style registries, plus TALA’s 37 ordered stages.
- Browser/WASM API coverage.
- Studio-specific behavior that needs replacement or explicit separation.
- A proposed implementation order and parity tests.

Two important findings: **TALA is now open source**, and **D2 already has structural source-editing operations in `d2oracle`** that the standard JS wrapper doesn’t expose. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

This is the investigation baseline. Next comes individual feature behavior and interaction tests, starting with source identity, inheritance, and editing semantics.

content.text:
ok I want to have the full reverse engineering of the d2, idea is to find all the element, all features and all parts of the d2 pipeline, and understand how to correctly port them to the web first, we dont want to have some side effects and so on right now which is not part of the d2

for that we need to make a surgery to d2, and then together map how each part will be implemented in the web

do you understand what I mean?

items.text:
Yes. You want to examine D2 itself before extending the editor further, then map its actual behavior into the web application.

That means tracing the whole pipeline: source syntax → parser and AST → imports and scopes → semantic compilation → diagram model → layout engines, including TALA → geometry and routing → rendering.

For each feature, we should identify:

- What D2 supports and how it behaves.
- Where that behavior lives in the source.
- What the browser/WASM API exposes.
- What React must implement to reproduce it faithfully.
- What cannot yet be reproduced, and why.
- How we will verify parity against D2.

This also means auditing our existing shortcuts—component presets, source overrides, manual positioning, edge routing, and rich-text rendering—for behavior introduced by the Studio rather than defined by D2.

The first deliverable should be a **source-backed architecture map and feature inventory**, followed by an implementation plan we review together. We should distinguish the open-source D2 pipeline from any TALA internals whose source is unavailable.

The current application is a prototype; it should not become the specification. D2’s implementation and observable behavior should define the specification.

content.text: I also want to be using tala engine, what do you use to render all of that?

items.text:
**TALA is now the default**, with your engine choice saved between visits.

TALA calculates layout; rendering is handled separately:

| Part | Renderer |
|---|---|
| Compilation and layout | `@d2lang/d2` WebAssembly + TALA |
| Architecture nodes | React DOM components |
| Markdown | `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm` |
| Code highlighting | `rehype-highlight` |
| Math | KaTeX |
| Connections | SVG using D2’s routes |
| Full-fidelity preview | D2’s native SVG renderer |

I fixed the reported Markdown/Python rendering and unfinished-block diagnostics. **React mode still doesn’t reproduce every D2 feature**; the separately labeled native preview provides the compiler’s complete rendering.

Published: [D2 Architecture Studio](https://d2-architecture-studio-aitemir.kuandikaytemir.chatgpt.site).
